fact.text: It first opened to the public on 24 February 2020 with the Namaste Trump event.
In 1995 it hosted Collision in Korea, the largest professional wrestling pay-per-view event ever.
Every home game since November 8, 1975 has drawn a crowd of over 100,000.
It was the first stadium to have its interior included in Google Street View.
MLS's Columbus Crew played here from 1996 to 1998, before their own stadium opened.
It began in 1904 when professor Edwin Kyle spent $650 of his own money on a grandstand from the fairgrounds.
Bear Bryant called it the worst place in the world for a visiting team: "It's like being inside a drum."
When funds ran out in 1921, students and faculty finished the original field themselves in two days.
It was dedicated to the 198,520 Texans who fought in World War I.
Bear Bryant's name was added in 1975, so he was one of the few Division I coaches to coach at a venue bearing his name.
